purpose: Runtime compatibility contract that EOReader 7 must satisfy for The Fold. Migration is in progress, not binary: browserEngineModules records what remains on the frozen /engine (legacy-eoreader6.1) mount; browserNativeModules records what has already crossed to the native /engine-v7 (eoreader7 native/) kernel, per the migrationLaw below. The 2026-08-29 pass (CLAUDE.md: "The connection pass" and its ratchet-completion follow-up) moved app.js's text organs and its operator/task-log algebra off /engine; emergence/tiers.js (and the nul/index.js statistics subsystem it stands on) is the one disclosed holdout — no native equivalent exists yet, and porting it faithfully is its own future pass, not a rider on this one.

Modules from eoreader7's native/ tree, consumed ONLY by this repo's own test/eval files today — never yet by app.js/serve.mjs/explore-server.mjs at runtime, per that spec's own disclosed scoping decision (live browser wiring needs a new server mount, a page-graph.mjs update, and a constitution.test.mjs II.13 allowance, none attempted this pass). migrationLaw: EOReader 7 must first satisfy this contract without requiring The Fold runtime changes.
Historical module paths may be implemented by a v6 compatibility facade over v7 internals.
Compatibility paths are removable only after The Fold has migrated that dependency to a canonical v7 API and equivalent behavior remains tested.
The contract describes required behavior and callable surfaces, not required v7 internal architecture.

A crossing is only real once measured: before app.js's import path moves, run the legacy and native implementations against the same real material and diff their outputs (parity), not just their exports (shape) — an export list matching is necessary, never sufficient.
